requirements.quote:
Each encryption level has separate secret values for protection of
   packets sent in each direction.
requirements.condition: When maintaining packet-protection secrets for multiple encryption levels.
requirements.required_behavior: Use secret values that are separate for each encryption level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse one encryption-level secret as the secret for another encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Exported or instrumented key schedules can be compared to ensure independently derived secret values are associated with distinct encryption levels.

requirements.quote:
Each encryption level has separate secret values for protection of
   packets sent in each direction.
requirements.condition: For packet protection within an encryption level.
requirements.required_behavior: Use separate secret values for the two packet-sending directions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the same directional traffic secret for packets sent by client and server.
requirements.why_checkable: Client-to-server and server-to-client traffic secrets at the same level can be obtained from test instrumentation and compared.

requirements.quote:
These traffic secrets are derived by
   TLS (see Section 7.1 of [TLS13]) and are used by QUIC for all
   encryption levels except the Initial encryption level.
requirements.condition: For every QUIC encryption level other than Initial.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the traffic secrets derived by TLS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not substitute independently generated non-TLS traffic secrets for those encryption levels.
requirements.why_checkable: TLS key-schedule outputs can be correlated with the secrets supplied to QUIC for each non-Initial encryption level.

requirements.quote:
The secrets
   for the Initial encryption level are computed based on the client's
   initial Destination Connection ID, as described in Section 5.2.
requirements.required_behavior: Base the computation on the client's initial Destination Connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not compute Initial secrets independently of the client's initial Destination Connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The dependency is stated, but this chunk omits the salt and exact derivation in Section 5.2, so it does not supply a complete expected-value check.

requirements.quote:
The keys used for packet protection are computed from the TLS secrets
   using the KDF provided by TLS.
requirements.condition: When deriving packet-protection keys from non-Initial TLS traffic secrets.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute the packet-protection keys from the TLS secrets using the KDF provided by TLS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not derive those packet-protection keys using an unrelated KDF or secret input.
requirements.why_checkable: Known TLS secrets can be injected and the implementation's derived packet-protection keys compared with the TLS KDF output.

requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.3, the HKDF-Expand-Label
   function described in Section 7.1 of [TLS13] is used with the hash
   function from the negotiated cipher suite.
requirements.condition: When deriving QUIC packet-protection material with TLS 1.3.
requirements.required_behavior: Use HKDF-Expand-Label as the KDF function.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different KDF function for TLS 1.3 QUIC packet-protection derivation.
requirements.why_checkable: Known-answer vectors can distinguish HKDF-Expand-Label output from other derivation functions.

requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.3, the HKDF-Expand-Label
   function described in Section 7.1 of [TLS13] is used with the hash
   function from the negotiated cipher suite.
requirements.condition: When applying HKDF-Expand-Label for a negotiated TLS 1.3 cipher suite.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the hash function associated with the negotiated cipher suite.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a hash function from a different cipher suite.
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiating suites with different hashes and checking derived outputs reveals whether the selected suite's hash is used.

requirements.quote:
All uses of HKDF-Expand-
   Label in QUIC use a zero-length Context.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not provide a non-empty Context.
requirements.why_checkable: KDF-call instrumentation or known-answer vectors can verify that the Context input is empty.

requirements.quote:
Note that labels, which are described using strings, are encoded as
   bytes using ASCII [ASCII] without quotes or any trailing NUL byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding a string label for a QUIC HKDF-Expand-Label invocation.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the label bytes using ASCII.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the label using a non-ASCII character encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact label byte sequence passed to the KDF can be inspected and compared with its ASCII encoding.

requirements.quote:
Note that labels, which are described using strings, are encoded as
   bytes using ASCII [ASCII] without quotes or any trailing NUL byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding a quoted string representation of a QUIC KDF label.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the surrounding quotation-mark bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The label byte string supplied to the KDF can be checked for leading or trailing quotation marks.

requirements.quote:
Note that labels, which are described using strings, are encoded as
   bytes using ASCII [ASCII] without quotes or any trailing NUL byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding a QUIC KDF label.
requirements.required_behavior: End the encoded byte string with the final label character.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not append a NUL byte to the label.
requirements.why_checkable: The KDF label input can be inspected for a trailing zero byte.

requirements.quote:
Other versions of TLS MUST provide a similar function in order to be
   used with QUIC.
requirements.condition: When using a TLS version other than TLS 1.3 with QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide a function similar to TLS 1.3 HKDF-Expand-Label for QUIC key derivation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the TLS version with QUIC if it lacks such a function.
requirements.why_checkable: The prerequisite is explicit, but 'similar function' is not defined precisely enough in this chunk to construct a deterministic conformance check.

requirements.quote:
The current encryption level secret and the label "quic key" are
   input to the KDF to produce the AEAD key;
requirements.condition: When deriving the AEAD key for an encryption level.
requirements.required_behavior: Input the current encryption-level secret and the ASCII label "quic key" to the KDF.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not derive the AEAD key with a different traffic secret or label.
requirements.why_checkable: Known secret inputs and KDF vectors can verify the exact label and secret used to produce the AEAD key.

requirements.quote:
the label "quic iv" is used
   to derive the Initialization Vector (IV); see Section 5.3.
requirements.condition: When deriving the packet-protection Initialization Vector.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the ASCII label "quic iv" in the KDF derivation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not derive the IV using a different label.
requirements.why_checkable: A known-answer derivation can verify that the IV output corresponds to the exact "quic iv" label.

requirements.quote:
The
   header protection key uses the "quic hp" label; see Section 5.4.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the ASCII label "quic hp" in the KDF derivation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not derive the header-protection key using a different label.
requirements.why_checkable: A known-answer derivation can verify that the header-protection key corresponds to the exact "quic hp" label.

requirements.quote:
Both "quic key" and "quic hp" are used to produce keys, so the Length
   provided to HKDF-Expand-Label along with these labels is determined
   by the size of keys in the AEAD or header protection algorithm.
requirements.condition: When invoking HKDF-Expand-Label with the "quic key" label.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Length to the key size of the selected AEAD algorithm.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not request an output length different from the AEAD key size.
requirements.why_checkable: The KDF output length can be compared directly with the selected AEAD algorithm's key size.

requirements.quote:
Both "quic key" and "quic hp" are used to produce keys, so the Length
   provided to HKDF-Expand-Label along with these labels is determined
   by the size of keys in the AEAD or header protection algorithm.
requirements.condition: When invoking HKDF-Expand-Label with the "quic hp" label.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Length to the key size of the selected header-protection algorithm.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not request an output length different from the header-protection key size.
requirements.why_checkable: The KDF output length can be compared directly with the selected header-protection algorithm's key size.

requirements.quote:
The
   Length provided with "quic iv" is the minimum length of the AEAD
   nonce or 8 bytes if that is larger; see [AEAD].
requirements.condition: When invoking HKDF-Expand-Label with the "quic iv" label.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Length to the larger of the AEAD's minimum nonce length and 8 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not request an IV length smaller than either the AEAD minimum nonce length or 8 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The requested KDF length is directly comparable with max(AEAD minimum nonce length, 8).

requirements.quote:
The KDF used for initial secrets is always the HKDF-Expand-Label
   function from TLS 1.3; see Section 5.2.
requirements.condition: When deriving QUIC Initial secrets, regardless of the negotiated TLS version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not replace it with a KDF from another TLS version.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial-secret known-answer vectors can verify that the TLS 1.3 HKDF-Expand-Label function is used.
